eyebrow: Code gets a commit hash -- data needs its own story

steps.label: Git keeps every version forever
steps.sub: fine for code, unworkable for gigabytes of data

steps.label: Git LFS stores large files outside git
steps.sub: tracks only a pointer in the repo

steps.label: DVC is built specifically for this
steps.sub: lightweight pointer in git, data in a remote

eyebrow: DVC: pin a commit, recover the exact data
code:
dvc add data/training_corpus/
git add data/training_corpus.dvc .gitignore
git commit -m "Track training corpus v3 with DVC"

dvc remote add -d storage s3://my-bucket/dvc-storage
dvc push

# Later, on an old commit:
git checkout <old-commit>
dvc pull   # fetches the exact data version for this commit
caption: The committed .dvc file is a content hash, not the data itself -- checking out old code also recovers old data.

eyebrow: Log the data version alongside the commit hash
caption: Now code, config, and data are all recoverable for any run -- without a manual note from whoever ran it.

subtitle: Closing Chapter 5: the norms that keep tracking, clusters, and data stores usable as more people share them.
